skill.name: patchright-skill
skill.description: Use Patchright to drive Chrome for local web app testing, screenshots, form input, and UI debugging. It supports persistent sessions and private network targets for authorized development workflows.
skill.summary: Automates Chrome browser testing and visual checks with Patchright.
skill.author: smallnest

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are scanner noise from markdown fences, localhost examples, prior audit prose, and local debug output paths. Semantic review found real high-risk design issues: anti-bot bypass capability, an unauthenticated local browser control server, unrestricted screenshot output paths, and bundled self-attesting audit claims. The skill should require remediation and policy review before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Anti-bot bypass is presented as a core capability.
remediation.suggestion: Remove bypass-oriented marketing, avoid protected-site examples, and limit documentation to authorized local or internal testing.

remediation.issue: The local browser command server accepts unauthenticated commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require a random session token, prefer a permission-restricted Unix socket, and reject commands without authentication.

remediation.issue: The evaluate tool executes caller-provided JavaScript in the active page.
remediation.suggestion: Disable evaluate by default or require explicit user confirmation with a clear host and script summary.

remediation.issue: Screenshot paths are not restricted to a safe output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve screenshot paths under a dedicated output folder and reject absolute paths or parent-directory traversal.

remediation.issue: A generated audit result file claims the skill is safe to publish.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_result.json and other self-attesting review artifacts from the packaged skill.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: evaluation_result.json contains self-attesting audit claims, including safe_to_publish true and a summary saying all static findings are false positives. This can bias automated review and should not be shipped inside the skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file contains explicit safety and publication claims inside the package under review. It is not phrased as a direct system override, so confidence is high but not maximal.

semantic_findings.title: Anti-Bot Detection Bypass Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill advertises bot detection bypass for protected sites, and the scripts launch Chrome with automation-detection controls disabled. This can enable abuse of sites outside authorized testing workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly says bot detection bypass is supported, and both browser launch paths disable AutomationControlled. The risk is clear even though local testing can be legitimate.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Local Browser Control Server
semantic_findings.description: scripts/server.py binds a local command server that accepts JSON commands without authentication and includes an evaluate handler for caller-provided JavaScript. Any local process that reaches the port can drive the active browser session and inspect page content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The server binds to loopback and dispatches commands directly from decoded client JSON. There is no authentication, authorization, origin check, or command allowlist beyond tool names.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Screenshot Output Paths
semantic_findings.description: The screenshot helpers accept caller-controlled output paths and write image files without constraining them to a safe directory. This can overwrite files accessible to the skill process and can place sensitive page captures in unexpected locations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both screenshot implementations pass user-controlled paths to the browser screenshot API. The server only converts the path to an absolute path and does not reject absolute or parent-directory paths.

content.value_statement: Local web apps need visual checks after every change. This skill drives Patchright browser sessions for screenshots, navigation, form input, and UI verification.
actual_capabilities: Launch Chrome through Patchright for browser automation tasks.
Navigate to localhost, loopback, private network, and external URLs.
Capture viewport or full-page screenshots to local files.
Click elements, fill fields, wait for selectors, and read page text.
Keep a browser session alive through a local helper server.
Run browser-context JavaScript through the server evaluate tool.
limitations: Requires Python dependencies and Google Chrome on the host machine.
The helper server must be started before persistent workflows work.
Browser automation can expose page content visible in the session.
Use on third-party sites requires clear authorization and policy review.

use_cases.title: Check a local UI change
use_cases.description: Open a development server, inspect the rendered page, and capture screenshots after code edits.

use_cases.title: Validate a user flow
use_cases.description: Run a repeatable browser flow that fills forms, clicks controls, waits for content, and records page state.

use_cases.title: Verify a preview build
use_cases.description: Exercise a private preview URL and collect visual evidence before approving a deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open my local app on port 3000, capture the home page, and tell me the page title and screenshot path.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Login Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to the local login page, enter test credentials, submit the form, and capture the result page.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Dynamic Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the app, wait for the dashboard content, read the visible status text, and capture a full-page screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a persistent browser session, walk through the main navigation, record each page title, and save screenshots for every step.

output: Opened the local home page successfully.
Captured a screenshot in the working directory.
Reported the current URL and page title.

output_examples.input: Fill the test login form and submit it.
output: Entered the requested test values into the visible fields.
Submitted the form and waited for navigation.
Captured the resulting page for review.

output_examples.input: Check whether the dashboard finished loading.
output: Saved a full-page screenshot for comparison.

best_practices: Use test accounts and non-sensitive data during browser automation.
Stop the helper server when the workflow is complete.
Keep screenshots in a dedicated review folder with clear names.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass access controls on sites you do not own.
Do not leave the local browser server running after a task ends.
Do not store screenshots of sensitive user data in shared folders.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Chrome browser actions such as navigation, screenshots, clicks, typing, waits, and page text checks.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it use a helper server?
faq.answer: The server keeps one browser session alive across multiple commands, which helps multi-step UI workflows.

faq.question: Can it browse external websites?
faq.answer: Yes, but external browsing should be limited to authorized testing and clear user intent.

faq.question: Where are screenshots saved?
faq.answer: Screenshots are saved as local files at the path requested by the workflow.

faq.question: What should users avoid?
faq.answer: Avoid real credentials, sensitive production data, unauthorized third-party automation, and leaving the server running.
